requirements.description: Digits 0 through 9 append correctly to the input display when pressed.
strengths: Buttons for digits 0 through 9 are correctly mapped to the digit method with their respective string values.
The digit method handles replacing initial zero/new input flags as well as appending subsequent digits properly.

requirements.description: Only one decimal point is allowed per operand.
strengths: The decimal method explicitly checks if '.' is already present in the current display value before appending a new decimal point.

requirements.description: Multi-digit numbers are supported and form correctly when consecutive digits are entered.
strengths: The digit method correctly handles string concatenation of consecutive digit inputs when self.new_input is False and the current display is not '0'.

requirements.description: Addition operation computes the sum of operands correctly.
strengths: The '+' button properly registers the addition operator via set_operator.
The calculate method defines the addition operation lambda: self.first + second which correctly computes the sum of the operands.
Operands are correctly parsed as floats before calculation.

requirements.description: Subtraction operation computes the difference of operands correctly.
strengths: Subtraction is correctly mapped using self.first - second in the operations dictionary.
Operands are properly parsed as floats.
Result formatting correctly handles integer representations.

requirements.description: Multiplication operation computes the product of operands correctly.
strengths: The multiplication operator '*' is mapped correctly to set_operator.
The calculate method implements multiplication using 'self.first * second'.

requirements.description: Division operation computes the quotient of operands correctly.
strengths: Division operation is correctly implemented using the '/' operator in the calculate method.
Handles division by zero properly with a ZeroDivisionError exception handler.
Maps the division button '/' cleanly to the set_operator function.

requirements.description: Clear (C) button resets all calculator state and display values.
strengths: The 'C' button is correctly mapped to the clear method in button_data.
The clear method resets the display value to '0', first operand to 0.0, operator to None, and new_input to True, fully resetting calculator state.

requirements.description: Delete (DEL) button removes the last entered character from the input display.
strengths: The DEL button is correctly mapped to the delete method.
The delete method properly slices off the last character using current[:-1] when length is greater than 1.
The delete method falls back to '0' and resets new_input when only one character remains.

requirements.description: Division by zero is detected before calculation and an error message is displayed instead of performing the calculation.
strengths: Division by zero is explicitly handled using a try-except block catching ZeroDivisionError.
An error message ('Cannot divide by zero') is displayed to the user upon division by zero.

requirements.description: Pressing '=' computes the result of the current expression.
strengths: The '=' button is successfully bound to the calculate method in button_data.
The calculate method properly evaluates the current expression based on the operator and operands.
Error handling for division by zero and unexpected exceptions is correctly implemented.

requirements.description: Results are formatted correctly and presented clearly on the display field.
strengths: Results are formatted by converting integer values to integer strings and keeping floats as-is
Display is updated properly via StringVar tied to the UI Entry widget
Exceptions such as division by zero and generic errors are caught and cleanly displayed
